title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Dead code cleanup, planned in batches
summary: Plan a Dead Code Cleanup turns the whole dead code sweep into reviewable batches, each cut with its proof and the commit that orphaned it, and Apply a Cleanup Batch removes one batch at a time.

highlights.title: Batches you can review
highlights.description: The sweep is simulated to its fixed point without touching a file, then cut into batches by module and size. Wave 1 holds what has zero references today, wave 2 what dies once wave 1 lands, each cut naming the earlier cut that orphaned it.

highlights.title: Proof per cut, counted for real
highlights.description: Every batch is a commit title and body with one proof line per cut and an rg command whose count is measured at HEAD: every file that names the cut is listed with what it is doing there, and a mention the detector cannot explain is marked for a human eye.

highlights.title: The cause from git
highlights.description: The last commit that removed a declaration's final caller names it, with its ticket, pull request and date. A batch mostly orphaned by one pull request takes its title from it.

sections.heading: Improvements
bullets: Added Plan a Dead Code Cleanup. It simulates Remove Everything Unused round by round in memory, without writing to your files, then saves `plan.md`, `plan.json` and one file per batch in the extension storage and opens the plan; Open the Cleanup Plan reopens it later without a new scan. Wave 1 holds what has zero references in the workspace as it stands. Wave 2 holds what only becomes dead once wave 1 is merged, each cut pointing at the earlier cut whose removed text named it.

Added a commit title and body to every batch file, with one proof line per cut in the detector's own terms, the channels the scan read and what it did not judge. The Verify it yourself section gives one rg command per cut with the count a reviewer will see: every other file that names the cut is listed and explained (a cut of this plan, a comment or a string, a homonym, a baseline entry, a source set no Gradle task compiles). A mention the detector did not count is marked NOT COUNTED, check it, and sends the batch to tier 2. Resource keys are searched qualified, as `R.string.x` or `@string/x`.

Kept together what has to leave together: an island and the declaration that held it, whatever family found that holder dead; a contract and its overrides; a key and its variants; a file and what it contained; an orphaned import and the cuts that orphaned it; and any two cuts of the same round where one names the other. A batch exceeds its size budget only when one such group is larger than the budget on its own.

Added git facts to the plan. The last commit that lowered the number of occurrences of a name removed its final caller, and its subject carries the ticket and the pull request. A name touched by a single commit is born dead. A merge without a common ancestor is a junction, and the symbol is older than the history. A move or a rename stays unattributed, because a wrong cause is worse than none. When one cause covers most of a batch, the batch is titled after it.

Added Apply a Cleanup Batch. It runs the real loop of Remove Everything Unused with the batch's keys as a filter: fresh offsets at every round, the real cascade, the guard against files that moved. It ends with the keys applied against the keys the plan promised. Git is read, never written: the branch and the commit stay yours. Settings shape the batches: `kotlinJump.cleanup.maxFilesPerBatch` (40), `kotlinJump.cleanup.maxLinesPerBatch` (1000), `kotlinJump.cleanup.groupBy` (by module or by cause) and `kotlinJump.cleanup.gitFacts`.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: Measured on a large Android project: about a thousand cuts in six rounds became 38 batches, none of wave 2 without its trigger. One batch applied alone, 121 keys promised and 121 applied, compiled with no new error. The simulation takes about three minutes, the git facts about seven, and both can be cancelled.
